standard_prerequisites.name: Elementary facts on associated and weakly associated primes, projectivity over a local ring, and the auto-associated criterion for projective modules

standard_prerequisites.use: These supply the local characterisation of weakly associated primes, the existence of an element of a prime ideal that is not a zerodivisor on a given module, discreteness of the fibres of an etale morphism, freeness of a projective module over a local ring, and the criterion that a non injective map of projective modules over an auto-associated ring can be detected after tensoring with the residue field.

core_obligations: Set up the etale local model: pick g as in the preliminary lemma, apply the local structure proposition to Spec(S_g) -> Spec(R) with the module N_g and the two primes, obtaining etale horizontal arrows and N' = N tensor_S S' projective over R'; define M', the fibrewise overlined rings and modules, transport WeakAss, WeakAss_R and Ass through the etale maps, and record the key observation that any prime of Ass of the fibre module over the base change lies in the closure of the fibre prime (proof lines 3770-3832).

Prove that q weakly associated to M tensor_R N forces the fibre prime to be associated to the fibre module: if not, the transported prime is not associated, so there is an element of it that is not a zerodivisor on the fibre module, universality of injectivity makes multiplication by a lift universally injective after localising at p', and hence the prime cannot be weakly associated to M' tensor_R' N' (proof lines 3834-3856).

Prove the same implication for the base prime: assume q weakly associated, pick z with q minimal over its annihilator, use the generators of p to produce elements g_i outside q with g_i f_i^{n_i} z = 0, and show f_i^{n_i} annihilates the localised image z'; the claim follows from the key observation plus universality of injectivity applied to g'_i. Then the annihilator of z' has radical p', so since N'_{p'} is free over the local ring R'_{p'} one finds a finite free direct summand carrying z', which forces p' and hence p to be weakly associated (proof lines 3858-3911).

Prove the converse: transport the situation once more so that p is weakly associated to M, the fibre prime is maximal among associated primes of the fibre module, N is projective over R, and R is local with maximal ideal p; choose y whose annihilator has radical p and generators of the fibre prime, consider the map N/IN -> (N/IN)^{direct sum n} given by multiplication by the g_i, use that its reduction modulo p is not injective and that R/I is auto-associated to conclude that it is itself not injective, take a nonzero z in its kernel, and apply the already proven direction to the ring map R -> S and the modules R/I and N to identify the minimal prime over the annihilator of z with q (proof lines 3913-3980).
proof_roadmap: Reduce to an etale local model where the flat module becomes projective and record the key observation on the associated primes of the fibre (proof lines 3770-3832).

Two forward implications: the fibre prime must be associated, and the base prime must be weakly associated, the second obtained by transferring a relation from the etale cover to a free direct summand (proof lines 3834-3911).

The converse by a five-condition reduction, a non injective map of projective modules over an auto-associated ring detected after tensoring with the residue field, and an application of the already proven direction (proof lines 3913-3980).
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises the weakly associated primes of M tensor_R N, for a finite presentation R -> S and a finitely presented S-module N flat over R, as the primes lying over a weakly associated prime of M at which the fibre prime is associated to the fibre of N (statement lines 3749-3768, tag 05IG). The proof is long and genuinely reduction driven: an etale local model makes N projective over the base, the key observation on the associated primes of the fibre is extracted, the two forward implications are proved by universality of injectivity together with the fact that the localised module becomes a finite free direct summand, and the converse needs a five-condition reduction plus the determination of non injectivity of a map of projective modules over an auto-associated ring after tensoring with the residue field. That last step is not a routine citation, so the claim is H2.
